newsitem.title: MOROCCO: King Hassan of Morocco to set up Al-Qods fund.
newsitem.headline: King Hassan of Morocco to set up Al-Qods fund.

text.p: King Hassan of Morocco, who presides at Al-Qods (Jerusalem) Committee, is expected to announce on Tuesday the setting up of a fund to provide financial support to the holy city and its Palestinian citizens.
Visiting Palestinian Finance Minister Mohammed Zuhdi al-Nashashibi told reporters on Monday that a meeting with King Hassan was scheduled for Tuesday afternoon in Rabat to discuss the issue.

"His Majesty King Hassan, who is the chairman of Al-Qods Committee, is expected to announce on Tuesday the setting up of Beit al-Mal institution to financially support Al-Qods and its citizens...Our meeting with the king will focus on this question," Nashashibi, who heads an official Palestinian delegation, said.
The move aims at halting what he called the judaisation of the holy city but he gave no details of the fund's initial capital.

Nashashibi, who held a working session with Moroccan Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj Monday, said: "Some 60,000 Palestinians who were born and live in Jerusalem were daily treated as foreigners by the Israeli administration."
"Time has come for the Moslem community to reinforce its material and moral support to the holy city which lacks basic health and education infrastructure," Nashashibi said.

The Palestinian delegation, which comprises Faycal al-Husseini, minister in charge of Jerusalem affairs, is expected to meet leaders of the Casablanca-based CGEM businessmen association to promote investments in the territories under the Palestinian authority, Nashashibi said.

"We plan also to set up another financial project called Jerusalem investment company with an initial $100 million capital...Arab private sector should contribute to it and raise the fund to $500 million in future," a senior Palestinian official said.
The Palestinian delegation is touring Arab countries to promote both projects, he added.
Last week, the Moroccan king called on the the Moslem world for an active solidarity with Al-Qods "to preserve" the holy city identity, defend its integrity and protect its monuments.

"It is necessary that the deployed political efforts and continuing resistance by the Moslem community are accompanied by other efforts...In this context we call today on Moslems and their elites for a financial support to reduce sufferings of Palestinians," the king has said.

As chairman of Al-Qods Committee and the Organisation of Islamic Conference, King Hassan earlier demanded the setting up of Beit al-Mal fund, which will enable Moslems around the world to participate financially "to support of their Palestinian brothers."

Al-Qods Committee, which held its 16th meeting in Morocco in March, called on Arabs and Islamic states -- which took steps towards establishing relations with Tel Aviv in the framework of the peace process -- "to revise their ties with Israel, including the closure of missions and offices."
It said the recommendation "will remain effective" until Israel respects United Nations resolutions related to the peace process and committments of Oslo and Madrid, MAP said.
Since its creation in 1976, Al-Qods Committee has held 16 sessions, 15 of them in Morocco under the chairmanship of King Hassan.

Members of the Al-Qods committee are Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Guinea, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Niger, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Pakistan, Senegal, Iraq, Syria, Mauritania and the Palestinian Authority.
